This catalog describes each research-motivated family without assuming access
to a private repository. A family can translate a public design, adapt a
working-paper design, or serve as a package benchmark. Its status and source
are stated below.

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from pypanelsim import designs
```

## At a glance

| Question | Family | Treatment timing | Main truth |
|---|---|---|---|
| How does TWFE weight dynamic cohort effects? | Baker | staggered cohorts | cohort-event effects |
| Can a joint test detect effect heterogeneity? | F-test | one or several cohorts | temporal or cohort surfaces |
| How much should event-study cohorts be pooled? | Lepskii | many staggered cohorts | support-aware cohort paths |
| What happens when parallel trends holds only conditionally? | ATT-DML | one cohort or clustered timing | ATT and conditional trends |
| Can small regression summaries preserve a large experiment? | regression compression | one or two cohorts | event-time effects and sufficient summaries |
| How do mixed panel structures affect a counterfactual estimator? | composite panel | one cohort | treated counterfactual surface |

## Baker dynamic effects

**Question.** Why can a two-way fixed-effects coefficient differ from the
average effect when cohorts adopt at different times and effects grow at
different rates?

**Law.** States enter one of three adoption cohorts. Untreated outcomes contain
state and year effects. A cohort's effect grows linearly with exposure length.

**Target.** The stored effect surface supplies cohort-event truth and the
treated-cell ATT.

```{python}
baker_panel = designs.baker(
    config=designs.BakerPanelConfig(n_units=200),
    seed=42,
)
print(baker_panel.shape, round(baker_panel.true_att, 3))
```

**Source.** This is a Python translation of Andrew Baker's public
[JFE_DID](https://github.com/andrewchbaker/JFE_DID) simulation. See [Baker TWFE
failure](vignettes/baker-twfe.qmd).

## F-test heterogeneity designs

**Question.** Can a joint test distinguish a common effect path from temporal
or cohort heterogeneity?

**Law.** The temporal family has one adoption date and seven effect paths. The
cohort family has three adoption cohorts and seven cohort-effect surfaces.
Untreated outcomes include fixed effects, trends, periodic components, and
correlated errors.

```{python}
print(designs.available_ftest_temporal_designs())
print(designs.available_ftest_cohort_designs())

ftest_panel = designs.ftest_cohort(
    "selection_on_gains",
    config=designs.FTestCohortConfig(n_units=240),
    seed=42,
)
print(ftest_panel.truth.att_by_cohort()["att"])
```

**Source.** The family follows the public
[TestingInEventStudies](https://github.com/apoorvalal/TestingInEventStudies)
project and its paper, [When can we get away with using the two-way fixed
effects regression?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05125). See [F-test
heterogeneity designs](vignettes/ftest-heterogeneity.qmd).

## Adaptive partial pooling

**Question.** Which cohorts have similar enough event-time paths to pool, and
which comparisons lack calendar-time support?

**Law.** Nine adoption cohorts receive paths that range from complete
homogeneity to cohort-specific signed shapes. Untreated outcomes combine fixed
effects, periodic time effects, and two-way correlated errors.

```{python}
print(designs.available_lepskii_designs())

lepskii_panel = designs.lepskii(
    "tensor_blocks",
    config=designs.LepskiiPanelConfig(n_units=360),
    seed=42,
)
cells = lepskii_panel.truth.cohort_event(event_times=(-2, -1, 0, 1, 2))
print(cells.keys())
```

**Status.** This family adapts an unpublished working-paper design. It is not
presented as a published-paper reproduction. See [Support-aware event
studies](vignettes/support-aware-event-studies.qmd).

## Conditional and latent trends

**Question.** Does an estimator recover the ATT when unconditional parallel
trends fails but a conditional or latent version holds?

**Law.** Five variants cover linear and nonlinear conditional trends, stable
and unstable latent trends, and clustered ARMA outcomes.

```{python}
print(designs.available_att_dml_designs())

conditional_panel = designs.att_dml(
    "conditional_parallel_trends_nonlinear",
    config=designs.ATTDMConditionalConfig(n_units=500),
    seed=42,
)
print(conditional_panel.unit_covariate_names[:5])
```

**Status.** These package designs isolate assumptions used in augmented
balancing and double-machine-learning work. The related public source is
[Augmented Balancing Estimators of the ATT](https://apoorvalal.github.io/files/papers/augbal.pdf).
See [Conditional and latent trends](vignettes/conditional-trends.qmd).

## Large-panel regression summaries

**Question.** Can an experiment be reduced to small regression summaries
without losing the treatment-effect signal?

**Law.** The main design combines fixed effects, unit trends, serially
correlated errors, and a configurable effect path. The Anscombe variants hold
selected summaries similar while changing unit, time, or cohort-time
structure.

```{python}
compression_panel = designs.regression_compression(
    config=designs.RegressionCompressionConfig(n_units=400),
    seed=42,
)
print(compression_panel.shape)
print(designs.available_anscombe_designs())
```

**Source.** This family is connected to [Large Scale Longitudinal
Experiments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09952) and its [public
code](https://github.com/py-econometrics/panel-at-scale-code). See [Large
panels and compressed regressions](vignettes/large-panels.qmd).

## Composite panel benchmark

**Question.** How does one estimator behave when untreated outcomes mix fixed
effects, factors, time-series persistence, and sparse donor structure?

```{python}
composite_panel = designs.gsynth_composite(
    config=designs.GSynthCompositeConfig(n_control=80, n_treated=20),
    seed=42,
)
print(composite_panel.metadata["outcome"]["model"])
```

**Status.** This is a package stress test assembled from primitives. It is not
a formal reproduction of a paper or another repository. See [Composite panel
benchmark](vignettes/composite-panels.qmd).

## One draw from each family

The gallery is descriptive, not an estimator comparison. Units are sorted by
adoption time so treatment timing and untreated structure can be read together.

```{python}
#| label: fig-research-design-gallery
#| fig-cap: "Observed outcome matrices from six research-motivated design families."
#| fig-alt: "Six heatmaps compare observed outcome structure across the Baker, F-test, Lepskii, conditional-trend, large-panel, and composite design families."

gallery = {
    "Baker dynamic effects": baker_panel,
    "F-test cohort surface": ftest_panel,
    "Adaptive pooling": lepskii_panel,
    "Conditional trends": conditional_panel,
    "Large-panel regression": compression_panel,
    "Composite benchmark": composite_panel,
}

figure, axes = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(13, 12), constrained_layout=True)
for axis, (label, draw) in zip(axes.ravel(), gallery.items(), strict=True):
    order = np.argsort(draw.adoption_times, kind="stable")
    image = axis.matshow(draw.outcome[order], aspect="auto", cmap="coolwarm")
    axis.set_title(label)
    axis.set_xlabel("period")
    axis.set_ylabel("units, sorted by adoption")
    figure.colorbar(image, ax=axis, fraction=0.035, pad=0.02)
plt.show()
```
